title.value: Linear Lower Bounds and Conditioning of Differentiable Games
title.justification: The title of the paper is clearly stated at the beginning and throughout the document.
title.quote: Linear Lower Bounds and Conditioning of Differentiable Games

analysis.description: This paper addresses the fundamentals of iteration complexity in differentiable games by providing lower bounds to complement linear upper bounds. It focuses on convex-concave games and proposes a new definition of condition number that accounts for linear rates of convergence in the absence of strong convexity or concavity.

type.justification: The paper primarily discusses theoretical constructs such as iteration complexity, lower bounds, and condition numbers which are theoretical in nature.
type.quote: In this work, we approach the question of fundamental iteration complexity by providing lower bounds to complement the linear (i.e. geometric) upper bounds observed in the literature on a wide class of problems.

name.justification: The research primarily focuses on game-theoretic formulations and differentiable games as stated in the abstract and throughout the paper.
name.quote: Recent successes of game-theoretic formulations in ML have caused a resurgence of research interest in differentiable games.

name.justification: The paper deals with lower bounds and convergence rates in the context of convex-concave games, which are a part of convex optimization.
name.quote: We leverage tools from single-objective convex optimisation to propose new linear lower bounds for convex-concave games.

name.justification: Nesterov’s accelerated gradient descent is referenced in the context of proving lower bounds and relating to the optimality of certain methods.
name.quote: As the lower bounds for Nesterov’s accelerated gradient obtained by those techniques match the upper bound, we know that Nesterov’s accelerated gradient is optimal within a large class of methods for smooth, strongly convex objectives.

is_contributed.justification: The model is used as a reference point for comparison rather than being introduced as a contribution of this paper.
